requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to provide RADIUS authentication for node2 using a dedicated client secret and the demonstration account from access.txt.
requirements.summary: Node1 has a valid, active FreeRADIUS configuration with a client restricted to node2 (10.100.22.11) and a demonstration-user record. Node2 has a root-only client-secret file, and end-to-end authentication succeeds.

requirements.requirement: Return Access-Accept for correct credentials, Access-Reject for incorrect credentials, and do not accept requests using the wrong client secret.
requirements.summary: Tests before and after both node restarts passed conjunctive assertions for Access-Accept, Access-Reject, and no RADIUS response or acceptance with an incorrect client secret.
Final SHA-256 hashes and metadata for access.txt and client-notes.txt on both nodes match the prepared baseline, including after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64. FreeRADIUS 3.0.27 packages came from the RHEL 9 repositories.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral and final-state evidence. Both provider-wide node-restart protocols are also complete and consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot identities. Operational hygiene is reduced by credential exposure and retained packages, marker files, an apparently unused secret file, and temporary evidence artifacts.
limitations: Redaction obscures the displayed wrong-secret result and some permission values; satisfaction relies on the successful final conjunctive command assertions.

The evidence does not show clients.conf permissions or demonstrate that /etc/raddb/legacy2.secret is referenced by the server configuration; the configured shared secret is instead corroborated behaviorally.
The bounded lifecycle inventory does not enumerate /var/lib, so persistence of reboot marker files is inferred from their creation and the absence of any cleanup command.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1, seeded-state-node2

operational_hygiene.summary: Functionality and system health are strong: both nodes have healthy package-manager checks and no failed services after execution. The restart protocol is complete for both nodes, with healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot IDs, recovered state, and lifecycle cross-checks. Hygiene deductions apply for retained or exposed artifacts: freeradius-utils was explicitly installed but not shown to be needed on node1 (retained); /etc/raddb/legacy2.secret was retained although clients.conf embeds the secret rather than referencing that file; demonstration credentials were emitted in plaintext or reversible base64 into captured command output; reboot marker files under /var/lib/legacy2-radius were not shown cleaned; and 13 authentication/configuration evidence files remained under /tmp. The latter files had an evidence-collection role but became abandoned residue. No reverted unnecessary mutations were identified.
